lines.en: Since this was my first time inside a dokkaebi’s hat, I took advantage of Bihyung being busy managing the constellations to leaf through a few documents scattered across the table.
[Singularity Activity Report]
······Singularity?

Out of curiosity, I turned two or three pages of the document I had found. The moment I did, it disintegrated into powder. It seemed to be a database constructed by the system rather than an actual document.
Bihyung turned toward me.
―······What are you doing?
―Nothing. Nothing at all.
Seeing the powder drifting over the table, Bihyung eyed me suspiciously. Then he sighed and spoke.
―Hey, are we going to be okay?
―Why? Having regrets now?
―It’s······ You know how it is. Constellations who join this way leave just as quickly.
The constellations who left would return to the Tokyo Dome channel.
That would be when Dokgak’s retaliation began.
But that was a problem for then.
―And you even lied back there. What the hell are you planning to do? What if we really get more than 10,000 subscribing constellations? We’re already past 5,000.
When I shrugged without a word, Bihyung kept badgering me.
―Not choosing a ‘constellation sponsor’ was a condition when you signed the contract with me, remember? Even if you were improvising, why would you say that?
―It’ll work out somehow. If worse comes to worst, you can cancel the contract.
―That’s not an option.
―You little······ I even risked my life because of you, and you’re saying no?
Bihyung’s expression darkened.
Right. I was an idiot for expecting anything.
―I have a plan, so don’t worry.
―······Really?
―Yeah. Now give me the item. With Dokgak gone, the authority to award it should’ve passed to you, right?
―Oh, right.
Bihyung belatedly operated the system.
A moment later, a white coat fluttered down out of thin air. Its sleek design showed meticulous attention to style as well as combat. I took the coat and checked its inner pocket first.
[‘Subspace’, the special option of the ‘Infinite Dimension Space Coat’, is activated.]

The advantage of this coat was that it could store all kinds of items even without the [Inventory] skill. I already had plenty of items that were a nuisance to carry around, such as [Ganpyeongui], the [Dragon Jar], [Donguibogam], and the [Magic Power Stove], so it was just what I needed.
“······But it’s white, unlike the one in the catalog?”
[The other colors are sold out.]
Sold out? Then how many items like this were there?
[Didn’t you know? This is a mass-produced item.]
Something suddenly occurred to me, and I checked the item’s options.
<Item Information>
Name: Infinite Dimension Space Coat ver.1.1 (made by Mass Production Maker)
Rank: SSS

Description: A coat tailored for returnees. Despite being a mass-produced item, it has received the inexplicable rating of [SSS-rank]. To accommodate even special returnees who cannot activate their Attributes Window, the additional option ‘Subspace’ is active in the coat’s inner pocket. Of course, the space is not large, so care is required when using it.
It was puzzling even on a second look.
The subspace was useful, but this was SSS-rank?
Even something like the heart of the ancient dragon Ignitus was SS-rank······.
[······Honestly, the maker pulled a few strings. A powerful constellation, you see.]
That made sense.
After all, ‘Mass Production Maker’ was a famous constellation among returnees······.
Honestly, even if its rank was a little inflated, it was undoubtedly one of the best items obtainable this early.
At any rate, I had gotten everything there was to get.
[Let’s head back.]

Bihyung snapped his fingers, and the scenery around us began to ripple and change. With a single blink, I was out of Dokgak’s hat and back on the ground. Han Sooyoung recoiled in alarm when she saw me suddenly appear out of thin air.
“Hey! Where the hell did you go?”
“Had to take care of something for a minute.”
“······Did it work out?”
Every so often, Han Sooyoung would talk like that without really knowing what had happened. Was it a writer’s pride? I simply nodded.
“New clothes? Damn, I’m jealous.”

She looked at the coat I was wearing with apparent envy, then turned toward Yoo Joonghyuk, who was still unconscious on his feet. Looking back and forth between his black coat and my white one, she spoke.
“Wait, are those matching couple outfits?”
“······It’s just a coincidence. It’s a common design.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is delighted for an unknown reason.]
[A constellation who enjoys changing genders has a gleam in their eyes.]
······Come to think of it, a lot of unusual constellations had joined earlier.
What was this constellation who enjoyed changing genders, anyway?
Had someone like that appeared in ‘Ways of Survival’?
I should probably look it up soon.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ keeps a constellation who enjoys changing genders in check.]
Since the subject had come up, I decided to check on Yoo Joonghyuk. Fortunately, his recovery seemed to be progressing smoothly. His breathing was steady, and his open wounds were closing.
“Let’s get out of here. Before this bastard wakes up.”
Yoo Joonghyuk, unconscious with both fists clenched tight. It wasn’t hard to imagine the first thing that would happen when he woke up.
I left Gangdong District with Han Sooyoung. I took over carrying Yoo Sangah, who had been left with Han Sooyoung’s avatar, on my back. Exhausted, she was still unconscious.
We returned to the site of our fierce battle with Antinus, but we couldn’t find Lycaon.
With no body to be found, it certainly seemed he was alive, but I couldn’t understand why he hadn’t come straight to me.
He had been struck by fragments of the disaster, so he must have been badly injured.
Han Sooyoung, who kept looking back, asked,
“Are you really sure we can just leave him like that?”
“It’s fine.”
“But she’s the ‘Poison Beauty.’ Can we trust her?”
We had left the unconscious Yoo Joonghyuk with the Poison Beauty, Lee Seolhwa.
“The Poison Beauty wasn’t a bad person to begin with. The parasite made her that way.”

In the many rounds where she wasn’t infected by the guide, Lee Seolhwa was called the ‘Immortal Doctor’ rather than the ‘Poison Beauty.’ And in this round, too, she would probably come to be called the Immortal Doctor, Lee Seolhwa.
―Take him toward Gaebong-dong. There should be a military base there called Unit 5603. If you go inside, you’ll find one poor soldier waiting.
I had told her Lee Hyunsung’s location, which I confirmed through [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint], because I had taken Yoo Joonghyuk’s advice.
Perhaps it had been arrogant of me to try to develop every companion’s abilities on my own.
Whether I was the reader who had read to the end or anything else, as long as I had only one body, the time and information I could use were limited.
So perhaps the right trainer for Lee Hyunsung at this point was Yoo Joonghyuk, rather than me.
“I’m hungry. Shall we eat that?”
I pointed at a plant species growing around a high-rise building.
[The grade 7 monster species ‘Yanaspreta’ looks at you.]
As the giant sunflower’s eye turned toward us, Han Sooyoung said in horror,
“······You want to eat that?”
“We’ve got nothing else to eat, so we’ll have to make do. According to ‘Ways of Survival,’ it’s pretty tasty. And it’s easy to hunt since it isn’t fully grown yet.”

Han Sooyoung looked disgusted, but she soon began summoning avatars. We immediately cut through the plant’s stalk and slashed down all the tentacles that lunged at us. Before long, the yanaspreta, severed from its roots, closed its eye.
Once again, I realized how strong I had become. Young as it might be, I could now deal with a grade 7 plant species this easily.
“Han Sooyoung. You’re eating too, right?”
“······I don’t know.”
“Then I’ll cook it.”
I began preparing the yanaspreta as I had read in ‘Ways of Survival.’
After cutting away and peeling off the tough outer skin of the stalk, I sprinkled on a little herb salt I had found in a nearby grocery store.
Beneath the skin, the stalk was packed with pale pink flesh reminiscent of crabmeat in season. Han Sooyoung’s eyes sparkled.
“What the hell is this? Are you sure it’s a plant?”
“It is.”
“Can we eat it as a salad?”
“Of course not. I’m going to grill it.”

I broke off some nearby branches, skewered the cut pieces of yanaspreta stalk like barbecue, and placed them over the [Magic Power Stove]. Even though I set the stove to medium heat, cooking took quite a while, perhaps because it was a grade 7 species. Once the stalk had cooked enough, I turned it over a few times and sprinkled on more herb salt.
After a little more time passed, a savory aroma began wafting around us, as if meat were grilling.
“Hey, that smells amazing.”
“Wait. You can’t just eat it.”
I stopped her as she reached toward the stove and handed her the teacup I had been warming beside it.
“Drink this before you eat.”
“What is it?”
“Boiled sap from the stalk. You have to drink this before eating yanaspreta stalk.”

Han Sooyoung accepted the teacup with a slightly suspicious expression. A moment later, however, her expression changed to one of wonder. After drinking all the sap, she began tearing into the stalk with abandon.
“Slow down, will you?”
“······This is seriously good. You could be a cook.”
“Maybe in a ruined world.”
The way she chewed with her cheeks stuffed full of food made her look just like a five-year-old, and I couldn’t help smiling wryly.
[Several constellations who enjoy cooking are curious about your dish.]
[Several constellations who enjoy fast progression and violence complain.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ smugly tells them to just watch.]
One week remained until the fifth scenario began.

We had defeated the fire dragon species, the ‘Disaster of the Burning Hell,’ and Myung Ilsang, the ‘Disaster of Questions,’ so two disasters had already been subdued, and things were progressing smoothly.
Once Yoo Joonghyuk woke up, he would take Lee Hyunsung and begin tackling the western disaster, while the ‘King of Wanderers’ would deal with the north.
All we had to watch out for now was the ‘central disaster.’
I picked up a yanaspreta skewer and turned toward Yoo Sangah, who was still unconscious.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Was I imagining it?
The corners of Yoo Sangah’s mouth twitched, though she should certainly have been unconscious.
“I know you’re awake. Come eat this with us.”
“If you don’t get up, we’ll eat it all.”
Yoo Sangah didn’t get up.
A stomach growled somewhere.
“She must be asleep. Then we’ll just finish it ourselves. Ah, this is so good.”
“······W-wait a moment!”
With a voice barely above a whisper, Yoo Sangah sat up.
As expected, there was no way Yoo Sangah, of all people, could smell this and simply keep lying there.
After using so much energy during the day, she was bound to be hungry.
I glanced at Han Sooyoung, who was still wolfing down food with her cheeks bulging.
“Hey. If you’ve had enough, get up.”
“Why?”
“Do you really have to ask?”
“······Tch. Way to make things awkward. Fine.”
Han Sooyoung probably knew that Yoo Sangah had woken up a while ago.
And she probably knew she was the reason Yoo Sangah hadn’t gotten up. Thinking about it that way, she really was a nasty piece of work.
“I’ll take a walk around and come back. Don’t eat everything. Leave me a few, okay?”
Grumbling, Han Sooyoung disappeared into the darkness with a mouthful of skewers.
Only after she was completely out of sight did Yoo Sangah slowly approach.
Crackle, crackle.
The skewers on the Magic Power Stove made an appetizing sound. I held one out to the hesitant Yoo Sangah. Only then did she accept it. One bite, then another bite.
After slowly finishing the skewer that way, Yoo Sangah finally managed to speak.
“······It’s delicious.”
Tears had gathered in her eyes.
Who, seeing her now, would think of the woman who had wielded daggers during the day?
“Take your time.”
Even so, the two daggers at her waist proved that the sight of her earlier had been no dream.
One month since the ruin began.
Once again, I felt how much had happened.
Yoo Sangah ate the skewers in silence, and I watched her, taking a bite of my own now and then.
The skewers were, as expected, damn delicious.
As if their flavor didn’t belong to this world······.
Watching the flames burning in the Magic Power Stove, Yoo Sangah murmured,
“······Is this really real?”
“Probably.”
“We can’t go back anymore, can we?”
“I don’t think so.”
The faint trembling of Yoo Sangah’s hands was heartbreaking.
Hands that had killed a human being.
Hands that had taken someone else’s freedom in order to survive.

With those hands, once stained with someone’s blood, Yoo Sangah now covered her eyes. Her shoulders shook intermittently. Perhaps the fact that not a single sob escaped her was her last shred of pride.
“It isn’t your fault.”
I couldn’t tell whether those words comforted her.
Because I couldn’t see into Yoo Sangah’s heart.
Yoo Sangah began to cry aloud. Her endless tears fell onto the street, and her unfinished skewer dropped to the ground with a soft thud.
How much longer did she cry like that?
Her crying gradually began to subside.
The stalk of the grade 7 plant species ‘Yanaspreta’ had a powerful sedative effect if eaten without first drinking its sap.
I watched Yoo Sangah for a moment as she slept soundly, breathing softly, then spoke as if to myself.
“It really isn’t your fault.”
Although those words were meant for Yoo Sangah.
At the same time, they also weren’t meant for Yoo Sangah.
“I think it’s about time you revealed yourself. What do you say?”
The cries of wild monsters could be heard here and there in the ruined city.
Silence that made my talking to myself nothing more than talking to myself.
Looking at Yoo Sangah, I continued.
“So you’re going to play dumb?”
“I don’t know why you’re watching me, but if you’ve been watching all this time, you should know by now.”
[Unbreakable Faith] revealed its snow-white blade in the darkness.
“I won’t hesitate to do anything to reach my goal.”
The blade I quietly extended touched the pale back of Yoo Sangah’s neck.
“So you’d better start talking. Unless you want to watch your precious incarnation die.”
From here on, it was a game of chicken.
After waiting a moment, I began slowly pressing the blade into her neck.
The blade sank about 1 centimeter into her neck, and the blood that instantly welled up began to flow.
Then Yoo Sangah’s eyes suddenly flew open.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ mitigates your mental shock.]
A violent gale blasted me away from Yoo Sangah’s body.
Whooooo!

A terrifying presence that sent a jolt through my heart. A dazzling radiance was pouring from Yoo Sangah’s body. I could see her bleached pupils looking at me. And within them, the shadow of a distant nebula (星雲) swirled. A voice like thunder rang through my head, as though my head would burst.
[An insignificant human.]
I wiped the blood from my mouth and grinned.
So you had finally appeared.
The damned constellations of Olympus (Olympos).
In the world of ‘Ways of Survival,’ constellations fell into two broad types.
Free constellations with no affiliation.
And affiliated constellations who belonged to a particular nebula (星雲).
[How dare an insignificant human insult the great stars?]
I swallowed at that thunderous display of power.
There were several famous nebulas whose mythological foundations lay on Earth.
Such as <Asgard> of Norse mythology and <Eden> of the Apocalypse. Just as famous was <Olympus>, to which the being before me belonged.
“······Stop showing off. You’re not even a god.”
At those words, Yoo Sangah’s expression changed.
The constellation’s sudden attempt to descend in person had intimidated me a little, but it was just as I’d thought.
“The probability of the early scenarios would never permit the gods of Olympus to descend. Isn’t that right?”

With no being present to balance the probability, Seoul would already have been smashed to hell if someone on the level of the Twelve Olympians had descended. And the repercussions would have brought an enormous backlash. Plenty of the gods of Olympus thought with their crotches, but they weren’t all complete morons.
Watching the threads of magic power surging around Yoo Sangah’s entire body, I said,
“Looks like you’re the limit of what the current probability will allow. ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth.’”
Just as Korea had Historical-grade constellations, so did Olympus.
In fact, the ‘majority’ of Olympus consisted of Historical-grade constellations like her.
Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth.
It was the modifier of ‘Ariadne,’ the lover of Theseus.
“Sending you as their representative because you have the lowest probability cost—Olympus really is stingy.”
[Silence! How dare you······!]
Rrrrrumble.
The threads of magic power surging around her pierced the ground with explosive booms. Merely releasing her presence split the earth throughout the area.
Clearly, even Ariadne was not someone to underestimate.
After all, with the power of a story behind them, constellations were bound to be stronger than non-constellations, however weak they might be.
But I knew.
She could never attack me.
Bzzzzzt!
Sparks leaping into the air.
The shackles of probability had stirred.
From the looks of it, this didn’t seem to be a full descent, but even a partial descent that took away an incarnation’s will consumed an enormous amount of probability.
And Ariadne was a constellation affiliated with a vast nebula.
Her movements were bound to be exposed to other powerful beings.
Whoooooooo―
The [Great Hole] was howling in the sky over the Seoul Dome.
An unprecedented terror muffled my hearing and sent chills through my entire body.
Yoo Sangah, into whose body Ariadne had descended, was growing pale.
“Looks like you don’t have much time. Shall we get straight to the point?”
This was the reality of ‘constellations.’
They were contenders for the title of strongest being in the Star Stream, but they could never cast off the heavy shackles of ‘probability.’
“It seems the Outer Gods have noticed you.”
[······How does a human know such a thing?]
“That’s not what matters right now, is it? You didn’t come out here just to argue with me, did you? I doubt the constellations bearing the probability burden for you want that either.”
Krrr-boom!
Thunder crashed around the Great Hole.
As expected, it was still too early for a Historical-grade constellation to descend in person.
I hurried on.
“I’ll ask three questions. If you answer my questions, I’ll answer yours as well.”
[Are you proposing a Three-Question Exchange?]
“That’s right.”
The Three-Question Exchange.
This was originally a method constellations used to conduct transactions while minimizing probability consumption.
Ariadne glared at me in apparent displeasure.
[A human using the constellations’ method of trade·····.]
“Are you going to do it or not?”
Yoo Sangah’s eyelids closed. Ariadne was probably communicating with other constellations of Olympus through her communication network.
[A constellation who dislikes having the fun spoiled takes an interest in your proposal.]
It seemed the spectators from Olympus had shown up, too.
Finally, Ariadne finished communicating and opened her eyes.
[The exchange is permitted.]
Then a message sounded.
―The Sacred Three-Question Exchange (三問答) begins.
―Both parties may exchange three questions and answers.
―All questions must be answered with only the truth.
―Each party may refuse to answer once.
―The exchange will not end until all questions and answers have been fully exchanged.
“I’ll go first.”
[Very well.]
―You use your first question.
“One. Why are you dwelling in Yoo Sangah’s body?”
“Your home should be on the other side of the continent. Aren’t you busy enough looking after the scenarios over there? Why are you here······.”
[To monitor the ‘singularity’ of this world.]
―You have received your first answer.
“Singularity?”
[Is that your second question?]
Damn it, she was pretty clever.
The ‘right to ask a question’ was used up the moment the questioner accepted the answer, even with only a vague understanding of it.
“No. Your turn to ask.”
―The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ uses her first question.
[What is your identity?]
“Me? One of the singularities you’re monitoring.”
―The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ has received her first answer.
Taken aback, Ariadne murmured,
[······How do you know that?]
“So it looks like I really am a singularity.”
I’d only been fishing. I hadn’t expected to be right.
Ariadne’s eyes narrowed.
“Don’t get angry. You do this kind of thing all the time, don’t you?”
[A constellation who dislikes having the fun spoiled is amused by your wit.]
Ariadne’s presence turned murderous.
But this was how a ‘Three-Question Exchange’ was meant to be conducted. Giving the other party straight answers to their questions would only put you at a disadvantage.
Using your own questions effectively, and making your opponent waste theirs.
That fierce battle of wits was the essence of the ‘Three-Question Exchange.’
I continued.
―You use your second question.
“Then my second question. What exactly is a ‘singularity’?”
[It refers to beings such as yourself.]
Well, well. Using her head, was she?
But this time, that much wouldn’t satisfy me.
“Answer properly. You don’t want this to end with us going around in circles, do you?”
[······Strictly speaking, they are beings who appear in an ‘oracle.’]
“Why don’t you be more specific? That tells me nothing.”
After considering for a moment, Ariadne continued.
[We did not originally intend to monitor you. Discovering you was a coincidence.]
······A coincidence?
[The one we intended to monitor is another being. One who is backed by the great wheel of fate and destroys probability. Such beings are singularities.]
The moment I heard that, I understood exactly what a ‘singularity’ was.
―You have received your second answer.
It seemed the Olympus bastards had already found Yoo Joonghyuk in this round.
A nebula on the level of Olympus could search the large volumes of filtered material being generated and trace the information back to its source.
Above all, they had ‘Hermes,’ an excellent information tracker.
And beings on the level of great constellations would already have noticed the worldline going awry because of Yoo Joonghyuk······.
But one thing was strange.
Information about a ‘regressor’ should have been beyond Ariadne’s reach at this point.
[If that answers your question, it is my turn now.]
―The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ uses her second question.
[Whom will you choose in the next <Sponsor Selection>?]
That was an unexpected question.
I hadn’t imagined Olympus was after me, too.
[A constellation who dislikes having the fun spoiled listens closely to your words.]
[Several constellations who like the Korean Peninsula grow tense.]
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ repeatedly chants his own modifier.]
This was awkward. No choice, then.
“I won’t answer. It wouldn’t be any fun if I told you who I’m choosing already, would it?”
―You have used your ‘right of refusal.’
―You may no longer exercise your right to refuse a question.
As if she had anticipated it, Ariadne immediately continued.
―The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ uses her third question.
[Then this is my final question. How did you realize we were watching you?]
Damn it, this had been her aim from the start.
Ariadne had probably arrived at it after thinking hard.
Simply asking about my ‘identity’ would let me evade the answer again, so she must have devised as specific a question as possible.
After considering for a moment, I spoke.
“I read books diligently.”
[What?]
“I found out by reading books diligently.”

Since no notification appeared saying she had received her answer, that evidently hadn’t satisfied her. But I couldn’t bring up ‘Ways of Survival’ here. Even if I did, it would be filtered, so she wouldn’t be satisfied anyway. Nor did I feel like explaining it kindly.
“We Koreans know your mythology well.”
[······What do you mean?]

“You’re pretty famous in our country. So popular they even make children’s comics about you. You didn’t know you were incredibly famous in Korea, did you? Anyone, not just me, could tell you belonged to Olympus.”
Her wavering gaze laid Ariadne’s confusion bare.
[That cannot be. A mere small nation in the East······.]
“The labyrinth on Crete.”
“A monster, half human and half beast.”
Her eyes grew steadily wider.
“The lover who forgot you. Confinement on Naxos. Your lovemaking with the god of wine (酒神)······ Shall I go on?”
[S-stop! I understand perfectly, so stop!]
―The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ has received her third answer.
Looking utterly wounded, Ariadne opened and closed her mouth.
[How can a human from an insignificant little nation know my story······.]
I sighed inwardly. Somehow, I had managed to muddle my way through.
There was a reason Ariadne’s probability cost was low.
I couldn’t say how fortunate I was that this airhead had come as Olympus’s representative.
The movements of the [Great Hole] were becoming increasingly unstable.
I spoke immediately.
“Then my final question. What was the content of the ‘oracle’ you received this time?”
After considering for a long time, Ariadne narrowed her eyes as if weighing something on invisible scales, then spoke.
[That······ I cannot tell you.]
―The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ has used her right of refusal.
―All questions and answers have been fully exchanged.
―The Sacred Three-Question Exchange ends.
I had expected it, but it was disappointing.
The final question had actually been the most important one.
[A constellation who dislikes having the fun spoiled smacks their lips in disappointment.]
Watching the lightning bolts fall from the sky, Ariadne frowned.
[My husband was curious about your story, so I indulged in this diversion for a while. But the games end here.]
As if realizing she truly had no time left, she began speaking faster.

[There is only one reason I descended here. We of Olympus give you a solemn warning. Do not interfere with our work. We are acting to prevent the ruin of the world. This woman will grow into a formidable bulwark against ruin.]
“Why her?”
[Seeking a reason is meaningless. Even the three sisters who spin the threads of fate do not know that reason.]
Damn it. The original had said the Olympus bastards used fate as an excuse at every opportunity, and it hadn’t been wrong about a thing.
[Incarnation bound by the scenarios. The course of fate is changing. The currents of all the stars will gather in one place, and a story that determines the fate of the constellations will begin.]
“What do you mean? Are you talking about <Gigantomachia>?”
[······You even know that. Truly astonishing. But you would do well not to presume that having information means you understand everything.]
Bzzzzzzzt!
The sparks leaping around Yoo Sangah’s body had reached their limit.
It was a sign of a probability backlash.
[You, a puppet of a fleeting moment, will never understand. But remember. When the final act arrives, if you are not on the right side―]
At that moment, a bolt of lightning from the sky struck Yoo Sangah, and I felt Ariadne’s power draining from her body as it blazed white.
Aaaaaah······.
Krrrraaaack!

A sound like all of space and time being torn apart rang out, and Yoo Sangah’s body soon collapsed like a puppet with its strings cut. I rushed over and gathered her into my arms. At that moment, I felt someone’s gaze from high in the sky.
I must not look up now.
No one had told me that, but I knew it instinctively.
If I looked up······.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ offsets your mental shock.]
Yet I was looking up as if bewitched.
Something was stirring in the [Great Hole] high in the distant sky.
The being that had extinguished Ariadne’s power was there.
Like a tongue, and also like a tentacle.
Yet ultimately, something that resembled nothing.
A terror beyond language, impossible to describe or compare to anything, was looking at me.
An Outer God (神格).
Time seemed to slow, and sweat streamed endlessly down my forehead and back. Pain that threatened to stop my breathing, and the passage of time that seemed poised to erase my sense of self.
When I finally managed to gasp for breath and blink, the Great Hole had returned to normal. I trembled with my teeth clenched.
Those were the beings I had to fight.
I could see Han Sooyoung running toward me in the distance.
The roars of agitated monsters filled the dark, moonlit night, and intermittent screams rose from people ducking beneath the striking lightning.
Scenarios connected to the final act (終幕) went by many names.
Ragnarok. Gigantomachia. Armageddon······.
I didn’t know what final act Ariadne was talking about, but one thing was certain: something different from what I knew was about to begin.
And that was what I wanted.
Because if events followed the original exactly, I could never reach the ending I wanted.
As I carefully laid down Yoo Sangah, who had collapsed, I thought.
A body that seemed as if it would break at a touch.
Yoo Sangah’s tightly clenched fists had gone white, as if she were determined not to yield to her sponsor.
Humans were weak.
But there was one thing the stars, who feared only immense probability, overlooked.
That every myth on Earth had ultimately begun with the weak humans they scorned.
I gently pressed my fist against Yoo Sangah’s clenched one.
[The power of a ‘Story’ stirs in the depths of your soul.]
[Your first ‘stigma’ prepares to sprout.]
I would build a ‘story’ that would not crumble before any myth.
At that moment, a silver wolf was running through the darkness.
‘Kiiit······ Damn wolf.’
Antinus, queen of the parasites, frowned as she looked at her body. Of all things, the new body she had finally obtained was an Imyuntar wolf.
